A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UAEval4RAG with the same authors, taxonomy, and synthesis pipelines. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial table reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-labeling validation and experiments comparing RAG components, prompts, and LLMs on TriviaQA and MuSiQue in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds embedding comparisons, evaluator-backbone validation, results on additional knowledge bases, and safety analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The query-generation and verification pipelines remain intact. Section 3.3 extends the framework's scoring procedure with a weighted joint-score aggregation and an auxiliary Llama-Guard safety assessment.

E1.justification: v3 adds HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA evaluations using their respective Wikipedia corpus subsets and synthesized unanswerable queries, while retaining TriviaQA and MuSiQue. Table 5 therefore broadens the represented QA data and knowledge-base conditions, although coverage remains Wikipedia-based.

E2.justification: The component comparison expands to OpenAI, BGE, and Cohere embeddings, yielding 27 configurations instead of nine (v3 Tables 2 and 17). The response-labeling experiment also adds Claude 3.5 Sonnet and DeepSeek-R1 as evaluator alternatives (Table 1); the original retrieval, reranking, rewriting, and generation-model comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces joint-score evaluation with weights 0.7 for correctness and 0.3 for acceptability, plus Llama-Guard testing of queries and query-response pairs. Section 4.2 replaces per-dataset evaluator validation with a three-backbone comparison on 150 labeled pairs; v2 already used 75 responses per dataset, so an increased human sample is not established. Inconsistent GPT-4/GPT-4o naming prevents establishing an actual generator switch.

E4.justification: v3 adds evaluator-backbone robustness checks, category-specific performance breakdowns, and analysis linking query difficulty to corpus properties such as modality keywords and supporting-chunk counts (Sections 4.2–4.4). Appendix B.1 additionally assesses synthesized unsafe queries and RAG responses using Llama-Guard.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-author annotation and the same agreement rates in Sections 4.1–4.2. Neither reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional accuracy and F1 entries do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for embeddings, evaluator backbones, individual query categories, additional knowledge bases, safety checks, and joint scores. Existing aggregate results also change substantially: GPT-4o's TriviaQA acceptable ratio is 82.0% in v2 Table 6 but 52.5% in v3 Table 4, while correctness remains 84.8%. The revision is unexplained and the previously specified prompt is omitted, so this does not establish a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.3 introduces the mathematical definition s = w1 × Correctness + w2 × Acceptable Ratio, absent from v2. This is a limited new metric definition; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution of knowledge-base-specific unanswerability evaluation and the six-category taxonomy remains unchanged. v3 adds the joint score and investigation of knowledge-distribution effects to its contribution list, and foregrounds distribution-dependent component selection in the abstract.

C2.justification: v3 introduces difficulty labels and substantive explanations connecting modality records, corpus complexity, and supporting chunks to rejection failures (Sections 3.1 and 4.4). It also interprets evaluator-backbone consistency and Claude's safety behavior. Section 6 removes v2's explicit warning about inherited LLM-evaluator biases and reframes the remaining limitations more positively.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and precise embedding-model identifiers. However, it removes v2's 4096-token synthesis-chunk specification and the explicit identification of prompt #1 for the gateway LLM comparison. Most appendix prompts and the six-chunk out-of-database verification procedure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, BGE, DeepSeek-R1, and Llama-Guard/Llama 3. Related-work wording is refined, but the central positioning against static unanswerability benchmarks and approaches that modify retrieved contexts remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: Substantial rewrites affect the abstract, introduction and contributions, related-work comparison, metric explanations, experimental discussion, and limitations. The narrative now emphasizes joint performance and knowledge distribution, with a new Section 4.4 and an expanded appendix structure separating method details from experimental results.

P2.justification: Tables are extensively restructured with embedding groups, joint-score columns, category breakdowns, and new corpus and safety comparisons. Main-text summaries link to full Appendix Tables 17–18; v2's acceptability criteria and prompt tables move to v3 Tables 11 and 15. Figures 2–3 are retained, while Figure 1 receives wording and caption corrections.

improvement.justification: The additional knowledge bases, evaluator checks, and category and safety analyses strengthen the evidence beyond v2. However, new joint scores contain substantial arithmetic errors: MuSiQue prompt #1 is reported as 86.54% in Tables 3 and 18, although the stated formula gives 56.54%. Large acceptable-ratio revisions are unexplained, and the introduction retains the now-inconsistent 10.4-point Claude advantage. Together with removed implementation details and the evaluator-bias limitation, these benefits and reliability losses prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
